title: The strangler pattern: migrating while production keeps running

videos.script: Lesson six said no to rewriting the reservation module from scratch. This lesson is what Coreto did instead. The seat holds move out of the monolith and into a new reservation service, while tickets keep selling every day. {{holds}} The method has a name. Martin Fowler called it the strangler fig, after a plant that grows around a tree until the tree is no longer needed. {{fig}} In software, something in front of the old system decides where each request goes. The new service takes the traffic one piece at a time, and every step can be reversed. {{facade}} We look at where to cut, how to route, and how to keep two stores of seat holds agreeing while both are live. {{seams}} Then the part nobody plans for. Coreto's new service carried ninety percent of the traffic after eight months. The last ten percent took four more. And the migration is finished only on the day the old code is deleted. {{tail}}
